column4: Unchanged: each phase leaves its artifact on the tracker, and AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and tasks.toml each carry or name a step, so an edit to any of them can drop or contradict that step.
Unchanged: the subject form and body rules break in the commit message, and prek.toml holds the hooks for five Confirmation rows, so removing a hook there falsifies the record.

Unchanged: every entry is a tool configuration, a place a lint flag can be passed, a configuration file that must not exist, or an inline exclusion, and each one's content can break the strictest-setting or one-location rule.
Unchanged: adding a file at any path that reaches no actor breaks the record, so ** stays honest for additions even though only .readers is bound for content.
Unchanged: the roster rows in this record, the CONTEXT.md anchors, the names in .readers and the check that compares them are all content that can break the roster.
Unchanged: the sufficiency and provenance rules bind every artifact purba writes, so every path and every written location stays in.

column3: Issue, Design spec, Pull request, Debrief
column4: Unchanged: issue bodies, specs and pull request bodies break the freeze in their own content, and AGENTS.md and the sign.yml thread are the carriers the Confirmation names as live.
Unchanged: a record that absorbs a second decision, or a title that stops stating one, breaks the rule in docs/decisions/, and AGENTS.md carries the rule.
Narrowed: the shell and Rust paths only say when test-first is owed, and the breach shows only in the implementation plan and the pull request's pushed heads, plus AGENTS.md which carries the rule.
Unchanged: the two-space style is stated once in .editorconfig, so only that file's content can break it.
Unchanged: the script's refusals, the sign.yml refusal, the ruleset's empty bypass list, the commit trailers and the fork pull request itself each hold part of the rule in their content.
Unchanged: a comment breaks the admission rule in its own text, and lychee.toml, check-links.sh and the generated marks in .gitattributes decide what the gated half reads.
Unchanged: record text breaks the section, numbering and citation rules, and check-records.sh is the command whose content decides them.

column3: Published comment, NOT-IN-GLOSSARY:wiki, NOT-IN-GLOSSARY:discussions, NOT-IN-GLOSSARY:public docs site
column4: Unchanged: each register file, the AGENTS.md closing section, the published-comment rule and the closed locations (opened by adding CHANGELOG.md, cliff.toml, a wiki, discussions or a docs site) can each break the record in their own content.
Unchanged: a gate over a judgement is wired in a workflow, a gate script, a task or the ruleset, so each one's content can break the rule.
Unchanged: a definition written into a record, or a glossary entry with an outbound link, breaks the rule in that file's content.
Unchanged: a widened GITHUB_TOKEN in a workflow, the failure reporter's token, the repository setting and the App's permissions each break the rule in their own content.
Unchanged: the trailers, the sign job and its scripts, the stewardship lines in CODEOWNERS, the ruleset and the sign-off setting each hold a liability statement that their content can break.
Unchanged: mise.toml, mise.lock, the linguist-generated marks, README's C toolchain line, each workflow's mise version and any devenv file can each break the single-manager rule in their content.
Unchanged: a package name in two of the three manifests breaks the rule, and check-manifests.sh is the comparison whose content decides it.
Unchanged: the pull request is where it answers one issue and says so when a second rides along, and no file is bound.
Unchanged: a script's placement and its callers' content in both halves break the rule, and CODEOWNERS must cover both directories by the record's own sentence.
Unchanged: record prose breaks the borrowed sentence rules, and check-records.sh is the command whose content refuses or reports them.
Unchanged: mise.toml, mise.lock, the generated marks, README's C toolchain line, build.yml's load check and any devenv file each break the rule in their content.
Unchanged: a nightly-only feature in src/ or Cargo.toml, the channel in mise.toml, and a fallback missing from the issue each break the rule in content.
Unchanged: the exact pins live in Cargo.toml and the one parsing module lives in src/, so both are bound by their content.
Unchanged: sign-branch.sh must claim no more than it checks, so its content is the one location that can break the record.
Unchanged: the five locations the record names each carry the floor, so a change to any one of them can break it.
Unchanged: script language, the .bats suffix, the build.yml Python exception, the bats roster entry, the test task and the hook globs are all content in these locations.
Narrowed: no record text can break the iff definition, which breaks only where CODEOWNERS and the ruleset route a record change to the code owner.
Unchanged: AGENTS.md carries the rule, and the pull request's own review history shows whether the agent answered first.
Unchanged: the crate-type and lint lines in Cargo.toml, the doc-test wiring in tasks.toml and quality.yml, and the Rust fences in *.rs are each content that can break the record.
Unchanged: the date in mise.toml and mise.lock, the absence of rust-toolchain.toml, bump.yml's proposal for a person, and build.yml's compiler line are each content that can break it.
Narrowed: no record text decides who owns a Decision Outcome, which the record makes true only through CODEOWNERS and the required code-owner review in the ruleset.
